description: The site must be edited for the target state to work: left as it is, a check, test, hook, build, installed environment or documented command would fail, or would run Deno where the target state runs Node or Turborepo, or would assume a per-package Python .venv or uv.lock. Examples: a new Deno.Command(...) call; a Deno.test(...) registration; Deno.execPath() spawned with 'run' or 'test'; a test asserting the text 'deno task backfire:install' in a message that the code changes; a deno.json task whose command must move to package.json or turbo.json; egg_base in a member pyproject; ready.py comparing sys.prefix with the package's own .venv; the commit-msg hook calling deno task commitlint. Takes precedence over can_stay when any part of the site must change. Excludes sites that only need deletion as a whole (use delete) and prose in historical records (use can_stay).

The site keeps working without an edit in the target state, or is outside the trial's scope. Examples: a Deno.readTextFile or Deno.env.get call that the @deno/shim-deno preload serves; import.meta.main; anything inside the shipped clean-code skill that stays on Deno; tools/spec-kit or tools/shellcheck paths; a test fixture string that merely contains the word deno as data and is not tied to a changed message; historical records in specs/ or .specify/. Does not apply when the site names a command, file or path that the target state removes or renames and a reader or check depends on it (use must_change).

The whole site becomes obsolete and should be removed rather than edited: a file or configuration entry whose job moves elsewhere. Examples: a per-package packages/<name>/uv.lock replaced by the root uv.lock; a deno.json top-level key such as nodeModulesDir or workspace whose job ends with the root deno.json; a .gitignore comment about Deno's cache. Use must_change instead when some of the site's content must be kept in a new form.

The evidence in the item is not enough to decide between the other classes, or the site is a governance or scope question that the user must decide (for example a sentence in AGENTS.md or the constitution naming deno task workflow).
